case_prompts.P01: Analyze why the original proof has long cases. How closely does decomposition by data constructors match the actual function's conditional branches? Which decomposition supplies the necessary recursive hypotheses and branch conditions together? After one normalization step, do the remaining goals in several cases have the same logical form? Choose and test a structure expected to close with the fewest extra splits and a shared set of rules. Do not spend the initial attempts merely shortening the original case-by-case script.
case_prompts.P02: Compare strengthening the proposition separately from choosing induction or case decomposition. For each decomposition, identify which recursive hypotheses and branch conditions are immediately available and which additional branches must be introduced. Distinguish assumptions needed by the current proof from assumptions required by the statement itself. Check preservation of the candidate property for every return form in the actual definition, including error and default-value branches. If a route that does not use an assumption appears viable, test it. Do not assume in advance that an assumption is unnecessary or that a particular induction scheme is optimal. Combine shared automation rules only after establishing the compositional property and decomposition.
case_prompts.P03: Does this statement require following the execution trace, or is a relation between final states sufficient? Look in the provided API for theorems connecting the current representation to another one. Compare the core operation laws and side conditions in each representation. Include the cost of converting back to the original goal when choosing the route with the fewest obligations. In particular, check whether the conditions needed for commutation follow from the meanings of the two input assumptions. Decide whether to retain induction based on this comparison.
case_prompts.P04: Before starting a long construction, compare a direct proof with provided library interfaces that could discharge most of the goal. For a library route, list differences in the conclusion separately from genuinely missing assumptions, and check what justified transformations could bridge them. If no interface is applicable, identify the exact unresolved premise and the evidence for that judgment. Validate the hardest bridge early. Do not treat a name, implicit-argument, or function-representation mismatch as mathematical impossibility. Also check whether an intermediate claim is more general than the final conclusion requires.
case_prompts.P05: Briefly compare how the equalities change representation from the core laws to the goal. Distinguish steps that obtain new information from steps that merely transport existing information. Look for separate expansions of both sides of the same equality, repeated normalization of the same large expression, and unnecessarily general intermediate results. At least one of the two routes should reduce these representation changes themselves, rather than only shortening the longest calculation block. Measure the cost of connecting the differential laws separately from the cost of normalizing the final scalar coefficients. After reconstruction, inspect the actual required types before sharing regularity witnesses. Judge high-level operators and low-level APIs by measured total cost, including the cost of connecting their representations.

controller_policy.early_diversity: By candidate 3, compile two routes that remove different obligations; a route may be tested by replacing one original block in a complete proof. A second route may be excluded by concrete type/definition evidence; do not force artificial diversity.
controller_policy.reconstruction: At least one complete reconstruction on a promising route; no mandatory quota of three competing rewrites.
controller_policy.diagnostic_gate: After two failures at one bridge, obtain its exact type/goal evidence before another repair. Do not abandon a mathematically viable route merely for syntax errors.
controller_policy.profiling: Provide the current candidate's profile promptly after a substantial rewrite with unfavorable heartbeat cost; use the same trigger and tool in all compared arms.
controller_policy.probe_accounting: Log read-only type inspection and optional standalone API probes separately from complete candidates; do not run unlogged or unbounded Lean searches. Under complete-proof-only evaluation, bridge probes consume candidate slots.
controller_policy.fair_comparison: Use identical original/context/tool feedback, candidate and monetary budgets, and fresh histories for comparison. Repeat runs when estimating reliability. Do not provide retrospective analyses or reference proofs to solving agents.
controller_policy.output_contract: Candidate JSON contains exactly one proof string. Keep any permitted brief notes separate. Validate and score with the fixed full-context evaluator.
controller_policy.objective_units: Proposed runner change: include rate r = baseline raw_hb / tokens and J for baseline, best, latest and each history entry, so the model does not recompute them.
controller_policy.token_profile: Proposed runner change: include per-line lexical token counts of the best candidate from evaluator/tokens.py, analogous to the heartbeat profile.
controller_policy.local_golf: Proposed runner change: after each new best, run the deterministic lexical rewrites locally (no API) and adopt the result if J falls; report applied rewrites in the next feedback.
controller_policy.packet_order: Proposed runner change: put the static problem and context before per-step fields so provider prompt caching covers them; canonical sort_keys currently places best/budget first.
